pride_data.title: Elucidating PTEN Conformational Dynamics and Phosphatase Regulation via Integrative Modeling and Mutation Prediction
pride_data.projectDescription: PTEN-WT and PTEN-4A models generation using Rosetta restrained with XL-MS crosslink distance restraints. Two major conformations of each protein were modeled
pride_data.sampleProcessingProtocol: For the in-gel digestion, the bands were cut to minimize excess polyacrylamide, divided into a number of smaller pieces. The gel pieces washed with water and dehydrated in acetonitrile. The bands were then reduced with DTT and alkylated with iodoacetamide prior to the in-gel digestion. All bands were digested in-gel using trypsin, by adding 5 Î¼L 10 ng/Î¼L trypsin or chymotrypsin in 50 mM ammonium bicarbonate and incubating overnight digestion at room temperature to achieve complete digestion. The peptides that were formed were extracted from the polyacrylamide in two aliquots of 30ÂµL 50% acetonitrile with 5% formic acid.  These extracts were combined and evaporated to <10 Î¼L in Speedvac and then resuspended in 1% acetic acid to make up a final volume of ~30 Î¼L for LC-MS analysis. The LC-MS system was a ThermoScientific Fusion Lumos tribrid mass spectrometer system. The HPLC column was a Dionex 15 cm x 75 Âµm id Acclaim Pepmap C18, 2Î¼m, 100 Ã… reversed- phase capillary chromatography column. Five Î¼L volumes of the extract were injected and the peptides eluted from the column by an acetonitrile/0.1% formic acid gradient at a flow rate of 0.3 Î¼L/min were introduced into the source of the mass spectrometer on-line. The microelectrospray ion source is operated at 2.5 kV. The digest was analyzed using the data dependent multitask capability of the instrument acquiring full scan mass spectra to determine peptide molecular weights and product ion spectra to determine amino acid sequence in successive instrument scans. These samples were also analyzed using a MS2-MS3 cross-linking methods.   This method involved a CID based MS2 fragmentation at a lower energy (25%) CID with high resolution detection in the Orbitrap (30000).  Peptides that have the DHSO diagnostic mass difference of 31.9721 Da were selected for an MS3 experiment performed in the ion trap.
pride_data.dataProcessingProtocol: These samples were also analyzed using a data dependent method as well as a MS2-MS3 cross-linking methods.   This method involved a CID based MS2 fragmentation at a lower energy (25%) CID with high resolution detection in the Orbitrap (30000).  Peptides that have the DSSO or DHSO diagnostic mass difference of 31.9721 Da were selected for an MS3 experiment performed in the ion trap.  For the data-dependent and XL-MS analysis, collected data were queried against the sequence of PTEN 4A mutant (P60484) using Sequest bundled into Proteome Discoverer 2.5 (ThermoScientific). Parameters included full tryptic peptides, 2 missed cleavages, protein acetylation at the N-terminus, methionine oxidation, DSSO modification of lysine residues (DSSO samples), and DMTMM (DHSO samples) as variable modifications, carbamidomethylation as a fixed modification, protein mass tolerance of 10 ppm, and fragment ion mass tolerance of 0.6 Da. Protein and peptide validation was performed using a decoy database strategy with Percolator with a peptide and protein level false discovery rate kept at <1% (see ref below) to identify high-confidence proteins. The criteria used for protein identification included at least two identified peptides, one unique peptide, and a Sequest score > 4.0. XL-MS data were analyzed using the XLinkX 2.2 (see ref below) node bundled with Proteome Discoverer 2.5. Parameters were as above with the addition of DSSO as the cross-linker and 3 missed cleavages. This data was searched against the human SwissProtKB database and specifically against the sequence of PTEN (P60484). Validation of cross-linked peptides was done using Percolator (Matrix Science) with an FDR set at 1%. A consensus workflow was also applied for the statistical arrangement; de-isotope and TopX filters were used to determine m/z error with selectivity set to ~10% FDR.  Each XL-MS spectra that were designated as high confidence were inspected for the following criteria; MS3 spectra from three of the four possible fragments need to contain sequence specific y and b ions consistent with the amino acid makeup of the peptide.  Sites of cross-linking were determined in XlinkX searches and manually validated.
